slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Palisade raise prices at 2027 renewals while churn rises, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR 15% with retention above 100%?
Where is churn rising, and is price the cause?
Which customers will accept a higher price in 2027?
What does each option add to 2027 ARR, and does it pass the 15% growth and 100% retention tests?
What will bring SMB churn down?
How do we roll the plan out in 2027, and what tells us it is working?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, with the leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall; Each price move rests on evidence for that segment
Leadership meeting, December 2026
New plans, such as a low-cost SMB tier; Enterprise contracts before renewal; New-customer sales targets

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay: 12% for mid-market, enterprise up to its caps, and SMB only after a test
Rising churn comes from 2025 promotion customers reaching full price: they explain 91% of the SMB rise
–	SMB churn outside the promotion moved only from 2.0% to 2.1% a month
Mid-market has shown it will pay more and enterprise rarely leaves, but SMB pricing is unproven with Inkwell at $9
–	Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
The CFO's 12% can add only $7.6M in 2027, and mid-market and enterprise rises alone clear the $98.9M target
–	Without any SMB rise, 2027 ARR still reaches about $99.03M
Activation is the lever on the promotion cohort's churn, but fixing it cuts SMB churn by up to a third, not half
–	Only 41% of promotion customers activated in month one, against 72% elsewhere
Approve in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and decide SMB in July
–	A Q1 test of +8% on non-promotion SMB renewals gates the July decision
